problems.source_says: The PDF explicitly reports 70 students involved in the experiment and links their 24 teams to 48 generated ideas. It describes evaluation and analysis of the team outputs, but does not separately identify the number of people represented in the final analysis, report exclusions or withdrawals, or provide a participant flow accounting. Thus 70 is supported as the reported study sample, but not explicitly verified as the final analyzed headcount under this challenge's standard. The form already acknowledges this reporting limitation; its numeric n_analyzed nevertheless treats that unverified analysis-stage count as known. The confirmed analysis-stage count should remain null. This does not establish that fewer than 50 people were analyzed.
problems.quote: The study involved 70 students in 24 teams, generating 48 unique ideas.
problems.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), Section 4.1, sample and consent paragraphs; PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Sections 4.2-5, output-level analysis; PDF p. 18 (printed p. 16), Tables 2-3; PDF pp. 28-29 (printed pp. xxvi-xxvii), Appendix 1. No separate analysis-stage people count appears in the full document.

confirmed.statement: S1 randomly assigned participants to the AI or control condition; the source gives no separately enumerated randomized headcount. The form's n_randomized=null is appropriately cautious.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 10), Section 4, experimental phases; PDF p. 25 (printed p. 23), Section 7, confirms participants were randomized.

confirmed.statement: The stated 70 counts students, 24 counts teams, and 48 counts generated ideas. Neither ideas, expert ratings, nor AI personas can be substituted for the people count.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), Section 4.1, sample paragraph; PDF p. 12 (printed p. 10), expert-evaluation phase; PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), AI-persona description.

confirmed.statement: No people counts by arm, whether randomized or analyzed, are reported. Both arms' null counts are supported by the reporting gap; an equal allocation must not be assumed.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 12-15 (printed pp. 10-13), Sections 4-4.2; PDF pp. 16-21 (printed pp. 14-19), results; PDF pp. 28-29, Appendix 1.

confirmed.statement: Participants could withdraw, but actual exclusions, withdrawals, and attrition counts are not supplied. The form correctly does not equate missing attrition information with zero attrition.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), Section 4.1, informed-consent paragraph; Sections 4-5 and Appendix 1 provide no participant flow accounting.

confirmed.statement: The description of three-person teams is inconsistent with the reported 70 students in 24 teams: 24 times 3 is 72. The paper does not explain the discrepancy, and the form already flags it; neither 72 participants nor two exclusions is established.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 10), Section 4; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 12), Section 4.1; PDF p. 26 (printed p. 24), Section 8.

confirmed.statement: The same teams produced proposals for both tasks, and the quality analyses combined the task datasets. These are repeated outputs from one experiment, not two independent samples; expert evaluation is the second phase, not another randomized participant study.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 10), Section 4, two experimental phases; PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Section 5, combined-task analysis.

confirmed.statement: The innovation-category analysis used only Task 1 ideas. This is an output restriction within S1, not a separately reported participant sample or evidence of participant attrition.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 17 (printed p. 15), Section 5, innovation-type analysis paragraph; PDF p. 20 (printed p. 18), innovation-category correlations.

confirmed.statement: Fifteen participants across three earlier usability studies are described as tool-development research. Their overlap with the experimental students is unstated, and no separate randomized creativity comparison is reported for them; they cannot be added to S1 to establish its analyzed sample size.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11), Section 4.1, opening paragraph; PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Section 4.2, usability tests and pilot studies.

confirmed.statement: The document does not identify reuse of S1 participants in another paper. The form correctly limits its claim to overlap not being stated; participant independence across papers is not established.
confirmed.locator: Full document, PDF pp. 1-41, including Section 4 on pp. 11-15, Appendix 1 on pp. 28-29, and references on pp. 30-39.

confirmed.statement: Tables 2-3 report statistical results without participant Ns. Appendix 1 contains four tool-interface screenshots and supplies no participant flow or additional sample counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 18 (printed p. 16), Tables 2-3, checked in PDF text; PDF pp. 28-29 (printed pp. xxvi-xxvii), Appendix 1, checked in PDF text and page renderings.

summary: The PDF reports 70 students in one randomized experiment but does not explicitly confirm the final analyzed headcount. Under the required explicit-support standard, n_analyzed=70 is unconfirmed and eligibility for at least 50 analyzed people remains unclear.
